title: Time-lapse imaging of Drosophila testis for monitoring actin dynamics and sperm release
protocol: Gently wipe the surface of the coverslip with lint-free tissue paper.
Place the dish on clean tissue paper.
Add 50–80 μL poly-L-Lysine in the cavity.
Leave undisturbed for 15–20 min.
Remove the poly-L-Lysine using a micropipette.
Give three quick washes using approximately 50 μL 1× PBS per wash.
Add fresh 1× PBS (80–100 μL) in the cavity as the live imaging medium.
Dilute the stock solutions by at least 100-folds in 1× PBS for preparing working solutions of drugs.
Prepare fresh working solutions immediately before use.
Use Rockout at an effective inhibitory concentration of 200 μM.
Use SMIFH2 at an effective inhibitory concentration of 25 μM.
Use Latrunculin A at an effective inhibitory concentration of 5 μM.
Use Latrunculin B at an effective inhibitory concentration of 10 μM.
Use Cytochalasin D at an effective inhibitory concentration of 2.5 μM and 20 μM.
Use Jasplakinolide at an effective inhibitory concentration of 50 μM.
Use Colchicine at an effective inhibitory concentration of 10 μM.
Use Taxol at an effective inhibitory concentration of 10 μM.
Use CK-666 at an effective inhibitory concentration of 250 μM.
Set the light path for the relevant fluorophores according to their excitation and emission bands.
Set the frame size to 512×512 pixels.
Make imaging mode simultaneous to increase time-resolution, unless there is bleed-through between the specific fluorophores used.
Use a laser line of 488 nm for excitation of GFP, dichroic FT of 500 nm, and emission band from 500 to 520 nm.
For combined imaging with GFP and dsRed labels, use lasers at 488 nm and 560 nm for simultaneous excitation.
Use a double dichroic filter set with FTs of 500/20 and 570/10, and emission bands from 500 to 520 nm and 570 to 590 nm respectively.
Set the required modalities depending on the type of experiment.
Initialize the stage for Multi-Area Time-Lapse imaging (MATL).
Activate relevant modules for laser ablation or Fluorescence-Recovery-After-Photobleaching (FRAP).
Fill the dissection cavity with 1× PBS.
Anesthetize Drosophila males using carbon dioxide or a cold plate.
Transfer the anesthetized flies onto the dissection cavity using forceps.
Place the dissection cavity under a stereoscope.
Wipe the forceps with lint-free tissue paper soaked in distilled water before starting and after each experiment.
Snip the abdomen of the fly using fine forceps (Dumont #55).
Disengage the pair of testes from the gut and cuticle.
Remove the rest of the body and wipe it on tissue paper.
Gently remove the accessory glands from the testes.
Separate the testes by pinching the connection between them.
Gently pick up the dissected testes using a pair of forceps and place them on the surface of the coverslip of the petri dish containing the imaging medium (1× PBS or 1× PBS+drug, as applicable).
Using the forceps, gently adjust the inherent coiled shape of the testes.
Ensure that the testis sticks to the poly-L-lysine coated surface.
Place the coiled base of the testis flat against the surface of the coverslip.
Soak a sheet of Whatman filter paper with PBS and place it at the side of the dish to maintain humidity in the chamber.
Seal the dish using Parafilm™ and place it on the microscope stage.
Identify the suitable samples using bright-field or DIC optics, which are appropriately mounted and appear intact, using a 10× objective.
Switch to the relevant higher objective according to the experimental requirement for documenting individualization and coiling events.
Use 10×, NA 0.5 or higher for high-resolution analysis of individualization.
Use 40×, NA 1.3 or higher for documenting sperm release events.
Use 20×, NA 0.7 or higher for actin cap dynamics and laser ablation.
Use 60×, NA 1.4 for Fluorescence Recovery After Photobleaching (FRAP).
Use 100×, NA 1.4 for FRAP.
Scan the specimen with wide-field epi-illumination before starting confocal imaging to locate the general region of interest within the testis.
Set the rest of the imaging parameters as detailed in subsequent steps.
Set digital zoom at 3× for high magnification imaging.
Adjust digital zoom or objective magnification for low magnification imaging as appropriate.
Set z-slice thickness at 0.5 Nyquist.
Set the number of z-steps with a buffer to capture moving NBs.
Set scan speed to 4 μ seconds/pixel or less.
Adjust frame iterations/time-resolution based on experimental requirements.
Use shorter time intervals for monitoring actin dynamics.
Use longer time intervals for monitoring gross morphological changes over hours.
Maintain laser power between 20–50 μWatts.
Set detector HV to 550–620.
Adjust detector Gain between 1 and 1.5.
Use an LED-based illumination system or Mercury-Halide illumination with a light guide for wide-field imaging.
Optimize the time interval as indicated in Table 1.
Maintain minimum possible laser power during sperm release and coiling experiments.
Follow conditions for FRAP and Laser ablation as indicated in Table 2.
Image multiple samples together using the multi-position module (MATL) for simultaneous xyzt image acquisition from multiple testis specimens.
